match_rule: EVERY signature keyword present case-insensitively in the finding body. rule_id is an ADDITIONAL constraint when both sides carry one, never a short-circuit. Neither path nor line is read: both are coordinates the reviewer chooses when citing an issue, not properties of the issue.

states.accepted: a finding the reviewer SHOULD produce. A miss costs recall.
states.rejected: a known false positive. A hit costs precision.
states.unreviewed: not adjudicated. Excluded from both numerator and denominator.

conversion_note: Converted by hand from ReviewBench's golden schema. ReviewBench's tp_fp 'tp' maps to 'accepted' and 'fp' maps to 'rejected' — an fp entry is a plausible claim its adjudicators judged not to be a real issue, which is exactly this bench's 'rejected' semantics. Signatures were authored by hand, not derived, because all 12 findings sit in two files and share vocabulary (fetch / page / commits / reviews / freshness); derived keywords would cross-match and the pilot exists to measure exactly that risk. No signature embeds a line reference.
